tagline: The Balearics and the Costa Brava — Mediterranean island-hopping at its densest.
summary: Spain's marine-mobility heartland is the Balearic Islands — Mallorca, Menorca and Ibiza with its sister isle Formentera — backed by the Costa Brava on the mainland. It is one of the Mediterranean's most concentrated marina markets, with world-class harbours and an affluent, design-led leisure clientele. Today the island-hopping and bay-to-bay flows run on ferries, charter yachts and water taxis. A clean, fast, stabilised foiling tier is the premium-but-practical layer this coast has never had.
why_marine_mobility: Spain's Balearic demand is dense and short-range: the iconic Ibiza–Formentera crossing, the bay-to-bay marina hops around Mallorca's Bay of Pollença and Bay of Palma, and Ibiza's San Antonio water-taxi corridors. These are exactly the legs a clean foiling shuttle is built for — short, scenic, high-frequency crossings run today on diesel ferries and charter boats. Navier's all-electric Pioneer II flies them smooth, dry and silent, riding the islands' existing marinas and harbours, with the Costa Brava and the longer inter-island legs as the natural extensions.

demand_signals.label: Affluent charter & marina market
demand_signals.note: The Balearics host one of the Mediterranean's densest concentrations of premium marinas and superyacht traffic, with marina operators such as d-marin active in the region — an affluent, recurring premium-water-mobility clientele.

demand_signals.label: Iconic island-hop volume
demand_signals.note: The Ibiza–Formentera crossing moves very large daily passenger volumes on conventional ferries — captive, high-frequency demand ripe for a clean premium tier.

demand_signals.label: Bay-to-bay marina density
demand_signals.note: Mallorca and Ibiza concentrate many marinas and harbours within a few nautical miles around bays such as Pollença, Alcúdia and Palma, where land transfers are slow and seasonal traffic heavy — a natural on-demand shuttle market.

use_cases.body: Ibiza to Formentera (La Savina): the iconic Balearic day crossing, flown smooth and dry on the all-electric Pioneer II as a clean, silent premium alternative to the diesel ferry.
Mallorca Bay of Pollença: Port de Pollença to Marina de Bonaire and the bay's marina belt — short premium transfers for an affluent charter-and-resort clientele on a clean foiling shuttle.
Ibiza's Sant Antoni bay: the Harbour One to San Antonio water-taxi corridor upgraded to a quiet, clean Pioneer II hop, matching a design-led leisure market with no comparable water product today.

navier_fit.pioneer_ii: Every featured leg sits well inside Pioneer II's 70-nautical-mile all-electric range: the Ibiza–Formentera crossing, the Mallorca bay-to-bay marina hops and the Ibiza water-taxi corridors are all commercial-ready today at 30 knots — clean, silent substitutes for diesel ferries and charter boats.
navier_fit.quanta_lr: The longer inter-island and mainland legs — Mallorca to Menorca or Ibiza (~25–50 nm of open water) and the Balearics-to-Costa-Brava mainland run (~100+ nm) — are Quanta-LR corridors (~700 nm hybrid range, H2 2026+), opening line-haul legs no battery day-boat can serve today.

signature_routes.label: Ibiza ↔ Formentera (La Savina) — the iconic Balearic day crossing
Mallorca — Port de Pollença ↔ Marina de Bonaire (Bay of Pollença)
Ibiza — Sant Antoni bay water-taxi corridor (Harbour One ↔ San Antonio)
Mallorca ↔ Menorca — inter-island Balearic crossing (no network leg yet)

transit_planning: For a marina group such as d-marin, a charter operator or a regional transport authority: a clean, fast, on-demand water tier layered onto the Mediterranean's densest marina market. Start with the proven intra-island Pioneer II hops around Ibiza/Formentera and Mallorca's bays — riding existing marinas and harbours with no new infrastructure — then add the longer inter-island (Mallorca–Menorca/Ibiza) and Costa Brava mainland trunks on Quanta-LR as range comes online.
competitive_landscape: Balearic travel runs on conventional diesel ferries (Baleària, Trasmediterránea and the Ibiza–Formentera operators), charter yachts and water taxis — reliable and affordable, but diesel, fixed-schedule and unremarkable. There is no clean, on-demand premium foiling tier. Navier's all-electric foiling craft is the missing option: faster and smoother than a ferry, cleaner and quieter than a diesel launch, and matched to a design-led luxury market that has no comparable water product today.
regulatory_note: Spanish maritime passenger transport is regulated nationally by the Dirección General de la Marina Mercante (Ministerio de Transportes) and Puertos del Estado; in the Balearics, the Govern de les Illes Balears and the Autoritat Portuària de Balears administer regional ports and concessions. Passenger operation requires vessel registration and crew certification — the regional port authority and Balearic government are natural first touchpoints.
seasonality: Peak demand runs the warm-Mediterranean high season (May–Sep), when island-hopping, charter and water-taxi traffic is heaviest and seas calmest; winter is quieter with more frontal weather and ferry disruption on the open inter-island legs. A stabilised foiling craft extends comfortable, reliable operation into the busy shoulder months (Apr/May and Sep/Oct).

precedents.what: Four Seasons Lake Austin operates an N30 in live luxury-hospitality service — proof of the premium resort water-shuttle model Navier brings to the Balearics' marina and charter market.
